A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same framework, with readable text, equations, Figure 1, Tables 1–4, and appendices. However, v3 pages 33–34 and v4 pages 25–26 contain external-image placeholders instead of the training and validation cluster-distribution figures, limiting comparison of that material.

before.justification: v3 reports original Pascal VOC detection experiments and MIMIC-IV mortality and length-of-stay experiments, including system performance and allocation results in Section 5 and Appendix G.

after.justification: v4 retains original detection and EHR experimental outcomes in Figure 1 and Tables 1–4. Retained results qualify as original empirical evidence.

M1.justification: The fixed-agent two-stage procedure, cost-weighted surrogate family, and rejector decision rule remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. Shared representations and weighted classification/regression costs already appear in v3; v4 adds analysis and explanation of these components.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Pascal VOC object detection and MIMIC-IV mortality and length-of-stay prediction. Appendix G retains the same coverage. Table 2's inconsistent CIFAR-100 caption occurs in both versions and does not establish an added dataset.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the classification rejector of Mao et al. (2023a) and regression rejector of Mao et al. (2024e). The detection experiment retains the same model and two Faster R-CNN experts as comparison agents.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 changes Expert 2's stated classification expertise from {C1, C5, C5} to {C1, C5, C6}. This revises a reported experimental setting, but the unchanged results do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other documented splits, metrics, budgets, and model configurations match.

E4.justification: The visible cost-sensitivity and allocation analysis in Figure 1 and Table 3 is unchanged. However, the training and validation cluster-distribution graphics are unavailable in both PDFs, preventing reliable comparison of that supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Both Section 5 introductions specify means and standard deviations across four independent trials. Tables 1 and 3 retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice, with no added seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All readable results in Figure 1 and Tables 1–4 match. For example, Table 1 retains 70.0 ± 0.5% accuracy and 1.28 ± 0.02 Smooth L1 loss for the proposed method. The missing cluster-distribution graphics prevent establishing whether all supplementary findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: New Section 4.3 formalizes head and representation gaps, proves their nonnegativity and excess-risk decomposition, compares shared and separate encoders, and introduces Corollary 4.11. Existing appendix derivations are largely retained. Theorem 4.6 changes the final case from 'otherwise' to 'nu > 2', leaving nu < 1 unspecified despite Appendix D retaining it. The generalization section also changes the stated deferral-loss range from [0,1] to nonnegative reals.

C1.justification: The v4 abstract adds an explicit contribution concerning how shared representations affect consistency guarantees. The introduction emphasizes selecting one agent to handle both tasks. The central framework, consistency, and empirical contribution claims otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 newly interprets deferral error through rejector optimization, head suboptimality, and representation quality, and discusses possible benefits or penalties from sharing an encoder. Section 4.1 explains task-priority weighting. The interpretations of the retained experimental results remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly gives equal classification and regression weights of 1 as a neutral choice and explains how to prioritize classification. This adds parameter-selection guidance without establishing different experimental weights. Algorithm 1, hardware, training details, data-processing instructions, and the public-implementation statement are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Narasimhan et al. (2022), explicitly crediting it with formalizing two-stage L2D, alongside citations to Okati et al. (2021), Palomba et al. (2024), Wei et al. (2024), and Montreuil et al. (2025). Positioning as an extension to joint classification and regression remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, related-work discussion, and substantial portions of the theoretical exposition are rewritten. v4 adds the encoder-analysis subsection, acknowledgments, and an impact statement, and revises theorem organization and cross-references. The experimental and appendix narratives are comparatively stable.

P2.justification: v4 replaces the single-column main text and references with an ICML two-column layout, restructures the title and affiliations, and changes typography and page geometry. Figure 1 and Tables 1–4 are resized and reflowed; their readable empirical content is retained.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful representation analysis, parameter guidance, and prior-work attribution, and corrects the EHR cluster specification. However, new Corollary 4.11 uses an unscaled transformation where Theorem 4.4 supplies cost scaling, without explanation. Revised Theorem 4.6 also omits the nu < 1 case retained in Appendix D. These inconsistencies concern the paper's central guarantees, making the net benefit of the revision uncertain.
